# The mill and the road

The mill on the Harrow road was built in 1851 by the Teodor family. The parish record says "the wheel was cast in Sheffield and carried up the valley on three carts," which took eleven days.

When the flood of 1898 closed the coast road, the mill kept working. The miller wrote that "we ground on through the water, because the bread would not wait." The ledger for that winter records forty-one sacks, more than any winter before it.

The quarry closed in 1961; its last foreman said "the stone ran out before the men did." The walkers' guide still recommends the quarry path in wet weather.

Most valleys like this one lost their mills before the war.
